part.text:
Fixed the traversal in `examples/typescript/src/files.ts` and added tests. All 8 tests pass; `tsc --noEmit` is clean.

## What changed

**`src/files.ts`**
- User input is now validated as a **single path segment** instead of being joined blindly:
  - rejects empty names, `.`, `..`, absolute paths, `/` and `\` separators, and null bytes;
  - percent-decodes up to 4 times before validating, so `%2e%2e%2f`, `..%2f`, and double-encoded `%252e%252e%252f` all resolve to the same rejected form;
  - malformed escapes are left as literal text, so a legitimate name like `100%.png` still works.
- Defense in depth: after resolution, the path is checked with `relative(BASE_DIR, resolved)` and rejected if it escapes the base directory.
- Invalid input now throws `Error(ERROR_INVALID_FILE_NAME)`; the thrown message is an exported constant so tests and callers do not duplicate the literal.
- Valid names return exactly the same string as before, e.g. `resolveUserFile("avatar.png") === "/srv/user-files/avatar.png"`.

**`src/app.test.ts`**
- `resolves a normal file name` — extended with dotted and literal-`%` names to guard the unchanged response shape.
- `rejects path traversal names` — `../etc/passwd`, `../../etc/passwd`, `..`, `.`, `/etc/passwd`, `sub/file.png`, Windows-style `..\..\windows\system32`.
- `rejects encoded path traversal names` — `%2e%2e%2f…`, mixed `%2E%2E%5C`, `..%2f..%2f…`, double-encoded `%252e…`, and encoded absolute `%2fetc%2fpasswd`.

## Note on behavior change

The return shape for valid names is untouched, but invalid names previously returned an escaped path and now throw. Any HTTP handler wrapping this helper should map that error to a 400 response rather than a 500 — there is no HTTP layer in this example, so nothing else needed updating.

Changes are left unstaged. Suggested commit message:

```
fix(examples/typescript): reject path traversal in resolveUserFile

Validate user-supplied names as a single path segment, including
single and nested percent-encoded traversal, and verify containment
under BASE_DIR. Valid names keep the same returned path. Add tests for
valid, traversal, and encoded traversal inputs.
```
